# The Residential Address

> The Residential Address helps non-US founders set up the US side of their business: a US residential address held under a signed lease, mail receipt and forwarding, US LLC formation, ITIN applications (IRS Form W-7) and guidance on opening US business bank accounts. Clients are founders in 40+ countries who own or are forming a US LLC.

Operated by Everest Ventures Group LLC (Florida, USA). Contact: support@theresidentialaddress.com, WhatsApp +1 647 436 7072.

## Services and pricing

- [US address for banking](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/us-address-for-banking.html): A US residential unit address held under a signed lease, with renter's insurance documents and mail handling, for non-US founders opening US bank, fintech and Stripe accounts. Not a CMRA or PO box. $2,000/year, no setup fee.
- [US residential address](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/#pricing): US residential address with a signed lease, renter's insurance and mail forwarding. $2,000/year, billed annually, no setup fee.
- [ITIN application](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/itin-application.html): Form W-7 preparation, review and filing. $700. IRS processing typically takes 7 to 11 weeks.
- [US LLC formation](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/llc-formation.html): LLC formation for non-residents, most often in Wyoming or Delaware.
- [Bank assistance](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/bank-assistance.html): Guidance on US business bank and payment processor applications for non-resident LLC owners.
- [US address service](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/us-address-service.html)

## Key guides

- [US LLC for Indian Founders: What You Need to Know](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/us-llc-for-indian-founders.html): Indian residents can own a US LLC. Indian side: FEMA overseas investment rules apply, LRS limit USD 250,000 per person per financial year, reporting through an AD bank (UIN, APR by 31 December). US side: EIN via Form SS-4 without SSN, Form 5472 with pro forma 1120 yearly ($25,000 penalty), US-India income tax treaty exists, no BOI filing for US-formed LLCs, ITIN optional.
- [Mercury Bank Address Requirements for a Non-Resident LLC](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/mercury-bank-non-resident-llc-address-requirements.html): Mercury requires a US-formed company with existing or planned US operations. The principal place of business can be US or international and residential, but not a registered agent, PO box or UPS Store address. Each 25%+ owner must give the physical home address where they live; mail drops, CMRAs and virtual addresses are not accepted. Documents: formation docs, EIN letter (or SS-4 with 90 days to provide EIN), government ID.
- [Stripe Account for a Non-US LLC Owner: Requirements and Common Issues](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/stripe-account-non-us-llc-owner.html): A non-US owner of a registered US LLC can usually open a US Stripe account. Stripe verifies the legal name, entity type, EIN, the representative's tax ID and a physical business address (no PO boxes). Without an SSN or ITIN, Stripe asks for a local non-US tax ID and proof the person is not a US taxpayer; owners may be asked for an SSN/ITIN after $500,000 lifetime volume.
- [How to Form a Wyoming LLC as a Non-Resident (2026 Cost and Steps)](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/wyoming-llc-for-non-residents.html): How non-US founders form a Wyoming LLC in 2026: $100 state fee, $60 annual report, registered agent, EIN, bank account and yearly filings.
- [What Is a CMRA Address and Why Do Banks Flag It?](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/what-is-a-cmra-address.html): A CMRA is a USPS Commercial Mail Receiving Agency, such as a virtual mailbox or UPS Store box. What it means, how banks detect it, and which addresses work for a US LLC.
- [How to Open a US Business Bank Account as a Non-Resident (2026 Guide)](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/how-to-open-us-business-bank-account-non-resident.html): What non-US founders need to open a US business bank account for their LLC in 2026: EIN, formation documents, passport, and the right addresses.
- [How to Get an ITIN as a Non-Resident: Form W-7 Step by Step](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/how-to-get-itin-non-resident.html): How non-US founders apply for an ITIN with Form W-7 in 2026: who qualifies, documents, Certifying Acceptance Agents, and the 7 to 11 week processing time.
- [How to Get an EIN Without an SSN or ITIN (Non-Resident Guide)](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/how-to-get-ein-without-ssn.html): Non-US founders can get an EIN for a US LLC without an SSN or ITIN by filing Form SS-4 by fax, mail or phone. Steps, timelines and common mistakes.
- [Form 5472 for Foreign-Owned Single-Member LLCs Explained](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/form-5472-foreign-owned-llc.html): Every foreign-owned single-member US LLC with related-party transactions must file Form 5472 with a pro forma Form 1120 each year. Deadline, penalty and how to file.
- [US LLC, EIN, ITIN and Banking FAQ for Non-US Founders](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/faq.html): Short answers on US LLCs, EINs, ITINs, banking, BOI and Form 5472 for non-US founders.
- [BOI Reporting for Non-Resident Owned US LLCs in 2026](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/boi-reporting-non-resident-llc-2026.html): FinCEN permanently exempted US-formed companies from BOI reporting in August 2026, including LLCs owned by non-US founders. What changed and what you still file.
- [Why virtual mailboxes cause bank rejections](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/why-virtual-mailboxes-cause-bank-rejections.html): How USPS CMRA listings affect US bank and fintech applications.
- [Wyoming vs Delaware for your LLC](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/wyoming-vs-delaware-llc.html)
- [Can you open a US LLC without living in America?](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/can-you-open-a-us-llc-without-living-in-america.html)
- [Best address options for non-US business owners](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/best-address-options-for-non-us-business-owners.html)
- [Registered agent vs business address](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/registered-agent-vs-business-address-explained.html)
- [Residential address vs virtual office](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/residential-address-vs-virtual-office-whats-the-difference.html)
- [Residential address vs PO box](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/residential-address-vs-po-box.html)
- [Best states to register an LLC in 2026](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/best-states-to-register-an-llc-in-2026.html)
- [Wyoming LLC address requirements](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/wyoming-llc-address-requirements.html)
- [Delaware LLC address requirements](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/delaware-llc-address-requirements.html)

## US LLC guides by state (for non-residents)

- [California](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/california-llc-for-non-residents.html): Non-US founders can form a California LLC by filing a $70 Form LLC-1 and a $20 Statement of Information, but every California LLC pays an $800 annual tax to the Franchise Tax Board.
- [Colorado](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/colorado-llc-for-non-residents.html): A non-resident can form a Colorado LLC online for $50 and keep it active with a $25 periodic report each year, plus a Colorado registered agent and the usual federal filings.
- [Delaware](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/delaware-llc-for-non-residents.html): Non-US founders can form a Delaware LLC by filing a $110 Certificate of Formation with a Delaware registered agent, then pay a $400 annual LLC tax every June 1 and file Form 5472 if foreign-owned and single-member.
- [Florida](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/florida-llc-for-non-residents.html): Non-US founders can form a Florida LLC on Sunbiz for $125, then file a $138.75 annual report between January 1 and May 1 each year and Form 5472 if foreign-owned and single-member.
- [Georgia](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/georgia-llc-for-non-residents.html): A non-resident can form a Georgia LLC for $110 including the service charge and must file a $60 annual registration between January 1 and April 1 each year.
- [Illinois](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/illinois-llc-for-non-residents.html): A non-resident can form an Illinois LLC for $150 with Form LLC-5.5 and must file a $75 annual report before the first day of the anniversary month each year.
- [Montana](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/montana-llc-for-non-residents.html): A non-resident can form a Montana LLC for $35 and must file an annual report between January 1 and April 15 each year, with member or manager names on the public record.
- [Nevada](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/nevada-llc-for-non-residents.html): Non-US founders can form a Nevada LLC for $425 in state fees (Articles, Initial List and State Business License), then pay $350 a year for the Annual List and license renewal and file Form 5472 if foreign-owned and single-member.
- [New Jersey](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/new-jersey-llc-for-non-residents.html): A non-resident can form a New Jersey LLC for $100, then registers for state taxes with Form NJ-REG and files a $75 annual report by the end of the formation anniversary month each year.
- [New Mexico](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/new-mexico-llc-for-non-residents.html): Non-US founders can form a New Mexico LLC online for a $50 Articles of Organization fee, with no state annual report afterwards, though federal filings such as Form 5472 still apply.
- [New York](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/new-york-llc-for-non-residents.html): Non-US founders can form a New York LLC by filing $200 Articles of Organization, publishing notice in two newspapers within 120 days and filing a $50 Certificate of Publication, then a $9 Biennial Statement every two years.
- [North Carolina](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/north-carolina-llc-for-non-residents.html): A non-resident can form a North Carolina LLC for $125 but pays a $200 annual report each April 15, and company officials appear in the public database.
- [South Dakota](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/south-dakota-llc-for-non-residents.html): A non-resident can form a South Dakota LLC online for $150, pays a $55 online annual report each year and owes no South Dakota income tax, while federal filings such as Form 5472 still apply.
- [Texas](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/texas-llc-for-non-residents.html): Non-US founders can form a Texas LLC by filing a $300 Certificate of Formation (Form 205), then file a franchise tax report or Public Information Report every May 15 and Form 5472 if foreign-owned and single-member.
- [Washington](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/washington-llc-for-non-residents.html): A non-resident can form a Washington LLC for $180 and must file a $70 annual report each year, but Washington lists governors publicly and has a gross receipts B&O tax, so it suits founders with real Washington activity.

## US LLC guides by founder's country

- [Australia](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/us-llc-for-australian-founders.html): Australian residents can form a US LLC without US residency; the ATO describes a US LLC as an entity Australia otherwise taxes as a company, with Division 830 foreign hybrid rules able to treat it as a partnership only when conditions are met, so Australian founders should get advice and still file US forms such as Form 5472.
- [Bangladesh](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/us-llc-for-bangladeshi-founders.html): Bangladeshi residents can own a US LLC with no US residency requirement, but sending capital abroad is tightly controlled by Bangladesh Bank under the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, 1947, so founders should confirm the permitted route with an authorized dealer bank before funding the LLC.
- [Brazil](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/us-llc-for-brazilian-founders.html): Brazilian residents can form a US LLC without US residency, but Brazil does not appear on the IRS list of US income tax treaty countries, and Brazil's Law 14.754/2023 sets specific rules for when profits of foreign entities controlled by Brazilian-resident individuals are taxed, so founders should get Brazilian tax advice alongside US filings like Form 5472.
- [Canada](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/us-llc-for-canadian-founders.html): Canadian residents can form a US LLC without US residency, but the CRA's longstanding position is that an LLC is a corporation for Canadian tax, which can clash with US flow-through treatment, so Canadian founders should get cross-border advice and watch both Form 5472 and Canadian foreign affiliate reporting.
- [Egypt](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/us-llc-for-egyptian-founders.html): Founders resident in Egypt can own a US LLC without US residency, the US and Egypt have an income tax treaty in force, and the LLC still needs an EIN, an annual Form 5472 if single-member and foreign-owned, plus Egyptian tax reporting confirmed with a local adviser.
- [Philippines](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/us-llc-for-filipino-founders.html): Filipino citizens living in the Philippines can own a US LLC, are taxed by the BIR on income from all sources under Section 23 of the Tax Code, benefit from an existing US-Philippines income tax treaty, and must file US Form 5472 yearly for a single-member LLC.
- [Germany](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/us-llc-for-german-founders.html): German residents can form a US LLC without US residency; Germany classifies a US LLC through a type comparison (Typenvergleich) based on a 2004 BMF letter rather than following the US tax election, so German founders need advice from a Steuerberater familiar with US entities and must still meet US filings such as Form 5472.
- [Indonesia](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/us-llc-for-indonesian-founders.html): Indonesian residents can own a US LLC, are generally taxed in Indonesia on income from inside and outside Indonesia with special rules for reinvested foreign dividends, have a US-Indonesia income tax treaty, and must file US Form 5472 yearly for a single-member LLC.
- [Kenya](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/us-llc-for-kenyan-founders.html): Kenyan residents can form a US LLC with no US residency requirement, but no US-Kenya income tax treaty is in force, the LLC must handle IRS filings such as the EIN and Form 5472, and owners should report to the Kenya Revenue Authority as their own situation requires.
- [Mexico](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/us-llc-for-mexican-founders.html): Mexican residents can form a US LLC without US residency and the US-Mexico income tax treaty is in force, but Mexico's Income Tax Law (articles 4-A and 4-B) makes Mexican residents pay tax on income earned through transparent foreign entities in proportion to their share, so founders should get Mexican tax advice and still meet US filings such as Form 5472.
- [Nepal](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/us-llc-for-nepali-founders.html): Nepali residents can be members of a US LLC under US law, but Nepal's Act Restricting Investment Abroad and Nepal Rastra Bank rules limit outward investment and there is no US-Nepal income tax treaty, so legal advice in Nepal should come before forming or funding the LLC.
- [Nigeria](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/us-llc-for-nigerian-founders.html): Founders resident in Nigeria can form and own a US LLC with no US citizenship or residency, but there is no US-Nigeria income tax treaty in force, the LLC has yearly IRS filings such as Form 5472, and Nigerian tax and CBN foreign exchange rules still apply at home.
- [Pakistan](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/us-llc-for-pakistani-founders.html): Pakistani residents can own a US LLC, but equity investment abroad is regulated by the State Bank of Pakistan's Foreign Exchange Manual, so founders should agree the funding route with an authorized dealer bank before capitalizing the LLC and then meet US Form 5472 and EIN requirements.
- [Saudi Arabia](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/us-llc-for-saudi-founders.html): Residents of Saudi Arabia can own a US LLC with no US residency requirement, no US-Saudi income tax treaty is in force, the LLC must meet IRS filings such as Form 5472, and zakat or income tax questions at home are handled by ZATCA and should be confirmed with a local adviser.
- [Sri Lanka](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/us-llc-for-sri-lankan-founders.html): Sri Lankan residents can own a US LLC, and outward investment under the Foreign Exchange Act No. 12 of 2017 is made through an Outward Investment Account with a licensed bank, within Central Bank of Sri Lanka limits, alongside US Form 5472 and EIN requirements.
- [Turkey](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/us-llc-for-turkish-founders.html): Founders living in Turkey can form a US LLC with no US residency, the US-Turkey income tax treaty is in force, and the LLC still needs an EIN and annual Form 5472 while the owner confirms Turkish reporting with a local adviser.
- [United Arab Emirates](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/us-llc-for-uae-founders.html): UAE residents of any nationality can form a US LLC, but there is no US-UAE income tax treaty in force, the LLC has US filings such as Form 5472, and the UAE corporate tax regime may be relevant if the business is run from the UAE.
- [United Kingdom](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/us-llc-for-uk-founders.html): UK residents can form and own a US LLC without US residency, but HMRC generally treats a US LLC as an opaque company while the IRS treats a foreign-owned single-member LLC as disregarded for income tax, so UK founders should get cross-border advice and still file Form 5472 each year.
- [Vietnam](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/us-llc-for-vietnamese-founders.html): Vietnamese residents can form a US LLC under US law, but no US-Vietnam income tax treaty is in force, the LLC has IRS filings such as Form 5472, and Vietnam's Law on Investment treats setting up a foreign company as outward investment with registration and capital account rules.

- [All state and country guides](https://www.theresidentialaddress.com/us-llc-guides-by-state-and-country.html)
